cultivar: Xiangbolü (also used as a cultivar name)
processing: Green tea made from one bud with two just-opening leaves of clonal bushes; the leaf is fixed, then shaped into tight, curved strips before drying.
harvest_season: Spring, picked at one bud and two just-opening leaves.
appearance_dry: Tight, curved strips, in the green shades typical of a Hunan spring tea.
appearance_liquor: Pale yellow-green and clear, as is typical of Hunan spring greens.
appearance_wet: Tender, even shoots, as is usual at this plucking standard.
taste_profile: No detailed tasting notes are on record; expect the fresh, gently vegetal sweetness typical of a Hunan spring green.

brewing.notes: General settings for a tender spring green. Leave the lid off so the leaf does not stew.

vintage_note: As with other Chinese spring greens, it is usually bought as the current year's spring harvest and drunk within the year. Nothing suggests it improves with age.
description:
Xiangbolü is a modern Hunan green tea that came out of the provincial tea research institute's experimental factory rather than from a village tradition. The name, roughly green waves of the Xiang, is also attached to a clonal cultivar, so check which one a label means.

The tea is made from one bud with two just-opening leaves. Its signature is in the shaping stage, which leaves tight, curved strips.

Detailed tasting notes are scarce. Treat it as you would any tender Hunan spring green: moderate water, a light hand, and an open vessel.

The same plant has also been used in research on black tea, with an orange-red cup and an orchid-led aroma. If you see Xiangbolü on an oxidised tea, that is the cultivar speaking, not this green.
history:
The tea was created in 1961 at the experimental factory of the Hunan Tea Research Institute. From 1982 it was repeatedly named a Hunan provincial famous tea, and in 1991 it took the Hunan agriculture department's Famous Tea Cup award.

A clonal cultivar under the same name carries the registration XPD028-2011. How the 1961 tea and the registered cultivar relate in detail is not clearly recorded.
